$comment: Build Spec §12, transcribed. Structure is axis -> pole -> sources.
The `frame` field on each pole is the owner's two-sentence framing (spec §12: 'Owner writes a
two-sentence frame per pole; the sources below carry the argument'). Those are EMPTY here and
render as a visible gap rather than being invented — see OWNER-DATA.md item OD-08.
URLs are absent for most items: the spec supplies titles and publishers, not links. Resolving
them is mechanical but must be done by hand to avoid citing the wrong piece, so they are left
null and the UI renders the citation as text rather than a dead link.
CURRICULUM BIAS WARNING (spec §12, ships in-product): the Redwood AI futurism reading list is
the backbone of several poles here, and its author states plainly that the selection reflects
her opinionated views, focuses on topics Redwood works on, and does not aim to be comprehensive.
Week 3 is entirely control; interpretability is nearly absent from the core; agent foundations
appears only in passing. The interp and agent-foundations sources below are deliberately drawn
from elsewhere to correct for this. The author also flags her governance recommendations as
significantly less confident, so the policy poles lean on 80k and emergingtechpolicy instead.
